tasks.spec:
You are making vehicle boarding and vehicle placement engine-correct in freytag-forge (Python 3.12). Working directory: /home/bcorfman/dev/freytag-forge. No network, no billed call, no uv: `export PYTHONPATH=/home/bcorfman/dev/freytag-forge TMPDIR=/tmp`, run `.venv/bin/python`. Do not git commit. YOU MAY EDIT: storygame/runtime/seating.py, storygame/runtime/jev_questions.py, storygame/runtime/capture.py, storygame/runtime/item_facts.py (only the protagonist-place landing code near `_apply_move`), data/stories/continuity-initiative/knowledge.yaml (ONLY adding one line to item k_sl_1a_a_r1), docs/world-model-grounding.md (replace only the existing Seats bullet text about vehicles, no other edits), tests/test_boarding.py, tests/test_vehicle_landing.py (NEW), and existing tests ONLY where a pin truly changes (list each). Never edit bench/frozen/, docs/testing-runbook.md; do not reformat unrelated text. Shared runtime has NO story names (no Kristin, truck, laptop, drawer, Michelle).

BACKGROUND (design from Brandon, 2026-10-24). The engine owns where the protagonist is. Three places are distinct: inside Michelle's house, outside (a separate area that contains the truck), and the truck (a vehicle inside the outside area, with seats). 'Go out to the truck' or similar MUST seat the protagonist in the vehicle. 'Go outside' must not seat her; 'Go inside' puts her in the house; both of those are already engine traversals (data/stories/continuity-initiative/connections.yaml, storygame/runtime/traversal.py), handled before boarding, so they never reach it. Getting out of the truck leaves her outside (the area of the seat). The vehicle's windows show the outside area, which the place-scoped prompt already handles (committed: storygame/runtime/knowledge.py / item_facts.py).

CHANGES.
1. Boarding means going to the vehicle again. In storygame/runtime/jev_questions.py change the `boards_vehicle` question text (keep the function and key names) to: instructions 'Decide whether the command has the player go to the vehicle, get into it, sit in it, or drive it.'; criteria true 'The command means going to the vehicle, getting into it, sitting in it, or driving it.'; false 'The command only looks at, touches, or talks about the vehicle, or leaves it.' (This restores the pre-change behavior that 'Go out to the truck' seats the player.) Contextual boarding in seating.board_vehicle (a bare 'Get in.' when exactly one boardable vehicle shares the protagonist's area) stays exactly as it is.
2. A command that only asks to board must not reach the narrator as a competing instruction. Live, after the engine seated the player, the narrator read the raw 'go out to the truck' as leaving the vehicle and wrote 'she gets out' (5 of 5 runs). Add a second Jev yes/no question in jev_questions.py, `only_boards_vehicle(ask, command, vehicle_name)`, key `only_boards_vehicle`: instructions 'Decide whether the command asks for nothing more than getting to or into the vehicle.'; true 'The command only goes to, gets into, or sits in the vehicle.'; false 'The command also asks for another action, such as driving, searching, looking, or talking.' In seating.board_vehicle (add a parameter for it, default None meaning keep today's behavior, and a new SeatingResult field `command_consumed: bool = False`) ask it only after a true boarding answer; when it is true, set `command_consumed` and make `command` equal the steps joined by spaces WITHOUT the raw command text; otherwise keep today's `steps + command`. Wire it in storygame/runtime/capture.py the same way boards_vehicle is wired, and make sure the steps still reach the narrator as the 'Just before this' line / command exactly as today. Record `command_consumed` in the capture record next to boarding_steps. 
3. Placing the protagonist in a vehicle puts her in a seat. In the place-landing code in item_facts.py, when a narrator reply places the PROTAGONIST at a name that resolves to a vehicle that has visible seats, the move target becomes that vehicle's first visible seat (sorted by id), exactly as board_vehicle does, instead of the seatless vehicle (the live game ended up with Kristin's parent = the truck itself 4 times). Non-protagonist things and vehicles without seats are unchanged. Keep any seated-use or notice behavior as is.
4. Data: in knowledge.yaml add the line `  reach_entity_ids: [back_door]` to item k_sl_1a_a_r1 only (the kitchen-evidence reveal), next to its other keys, so its beat is not offered while the protagonist is outside.

TESTS FIRST (tests/test_boarding.py and tests/test_vehicle_landing.py; small and complete). (a) 'Go out to Kristin's truck.' from the house with the boards answer true seats her (steps: enter text, laptop notice); (b) with only_boards true the resulting command equals the two steps with no raw command; with only_boards false the command is steps + raw command ('Drive Kristin's truck.'); (c) 'Look at Kristin's truck.' (boards false) does nothing; (d) get out: with the protagonist in truck_driver_seat the existing stand_before_leave with a true answer for 'Get out of the truck.' puts her in the seat's area (outside_house) and emits the seat's leave text; (e) vehicle landing: an item_facts reply placing the protagonist at "Kristin's truck" lands her in truck_driver_seat; a reply placing her at 'outside the house' lands her in outside_house; a non-protagonist item placed at the truck is unchanged; (f) a SYNTHETIC second vehicle (a boat with a seat; reuse the helper you or the previous boarding tests used) proves 1 to 3 have no truck-specific logic; (g) with the card recovered and Kristin at outside_house, 'Search the kitchen.' offers no candidate for k_sl_1a_a_r1 (reach) and in the kitchen it does. Update the existing boarding tests only where the wording/flow pins changed.

FINISH: ruff format and ruff check every .py you touched; run the focused suites in the check; report every existing test changed and why.
